resources.string: It will arrive when %s is back
It will arrive when your computers are back
Only text and images can be sent
Copy on the phone, paste on the PC. No account, no cloud: just your Wi-Fi. Open paste-get on the computer: it shows a code to scan.
Same Wi-Fi? paste-get must be running on the computer. A guest network or the computer\'s firewall can keep them apart.
Copy anything: it\'s on your computer in a moment.
Send with the button below, the Quick Settings tile, or Share → Send to PC.
Turn on Send what you copy
Scan the code shown by paste-get on your computer
This is not a paste-get pairing code
This phone is already paired with it, as %s. Pairing again replaces that pairing.
Once paired, this computer receives what you send from this phone.
Only continue if this code is on your computer\'s screen right now.
This code can\'t be used. On the computer, show a new pairing code and scan it.

The phone couldn\'t reach the computer. Check that both are on the same Wi-Fi and that paste-get is open on the computer, then scan the code again. A guest network or the computer\'s firewall can block it.
The computer refused the pairing: the code may have expired or been used already. Show a new code on the computer and scan it.
The pairing couldn\'t be saved on this phone. Free some storage, then scan the code again.
Something went wrong. Scan the code again; if it keeps failing, include the details below in your report.
Where this phone dials it, the last one that worked first. paste-get also finds it on the local network when its address changes.
%1$s will stop receiving what you copy, and this phone will stop connecting to it. To use it again, pair again. On the computer, this phone stays listed until you forget it there too.
Take a screenshot, paste it on your computer
On: each new screenshot goes to your computers\' clipboard, ready to paste. To see them, paste-get needs access to all your photos; it only ever reads new screenshots.
What paste-get needs to see each new screenshot.
New screenshots are never among them, so paste-get can\'t see them.
When Android asks, choose Allow all.
paste-get only sees the photos you picked. Allow all photos to see new screenshots.
paste-get needs access to your photos to see new screenshots.
Keeping what you copy comes next. For now, this lists what was sent and received since paste-get started: its kind, size and time, never the contents.
Nothing yet. What you send or receive shows here, with where it went and how fast.
Your computers know this phone by this ID, which comes from its key.
The colors of your wallpaper. Off: paste-get\'s indigo.
paste-get follows the phone\'s language. You can choose another one for it alone.
Send clipboard sends what you copied, from any app, in one tap.
Open Quick Settings, tap the pencil, then drag Send clipboard in.
The tile is already in Quick Settings
Free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 or later. No ads, no account, no data collection.
paste-get is built with these libraries. Thanks to their authors.
paste-get\'s core in Rust and its crates (rustls, tokio, prost, UniFFI…)
Mostly MIT or Apache-2.0; each crate\'s licence is checked to be GPL-compatible (cargo-deny)

Off: nothing you copy leaves the phone. On: each text you copy goes to your computers by itself. Passwords copied from a password manager are marked sensitive, and computers keep them out of their clipboard history.
Android\'s wireless debugging starts a small helper that sees copies. No other app, and it starts again by itself after a restart, on Wi-Fi.
The free Shizuku app lends paste-get the rights it needs. Start Shizuku again after each restart.
The system log says when you copy; a window shows for a moment to read it, which may close the keyboard.
Copy on the phone, paste on your computer, no tap
The built-in mode reads copies by itself, with no other app, and starts again after a restart of the phone. Setting it up takes a few minutes, once.
The set-up asks for a code in a notification, and paste-get\'s notifications are off. Allow them first.
Set-up under way: the pairing code is still to type.
Built-in mode: waiting for Wi-Fi (wireless debugging needs it).
Tap Pair device with pairing code in Wireless debugging, then type the 6-digit code here.
Step 1 of 3: looking for the pairing code screen…
Step 3 of 3: getting permission to switch wireless debugging…
Didn\'t work: %s. Try again with a new code.
the pairing code screen wasn\'t found: keep it open while you type the code
turn on Wireless debugging in Developer options
wireless debugging didn\'t start. Is it allowed on this Wi-Fi?
wireless debugging no longer knows paste-get: pair again
Once, in a few minutes. Then each text you copy goes to your computers by itself, even after a restart: Android\'s wireless debugging starts a small helper. No other app, no computer needed.
Shizuku already sends your copies. Set this up to stop starting Shizuku again after each restart.
Wireless debugging only works on Wi-Fi.
Allowed: the code is typed in paste-get\'s notification.
On Xiaomi phones, if paste-get\'s notification has no field for the code: in Settings, search for Notification style and choose Android. Or use split screen, at the last step.
In Settings → About phone, tap OS version (or MIUI version) 7 times, until a message says you are a developer. Android may ask for your PIN.
In Settings → About phone, tap Build number 7 times (on some phones it\'s under Software information), until a message says you are a developer. Android may ask for your PIN.
In Settings → Additional settings → Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging and allow it on this network.
In Developer options (Settings → System), turn on Wireless debugging and allow it on this network.
Tap Wireless debugging, then Pair device with pairing code. Without leaving the code screen, pull down the notifications and type the 6 digits in paste-get\'s notification.
In Settings, beside paste-get: tap Wireless debugging, then Pair device with pairing code. Type the 6 digits here.

Open recent apps and put paste-get in split screen (on some phones, long-press its card). Back here, tap Open Wireless debugging: Settings opens in the other half, and you type the code in paste-get, with no notification.
Getting permission to start by itself
Wrong or expired code. Tap Pair device with pairing code again for a new one.
The code screen was closed. Keep it open while you type the code.
Paired, but Wireless debugging didn\'t answer. Check that it\'s still on, then try again with a new code.
That didn\'t work. Try again with a new code; if it keeps failing, include the details in your report.
Each text you copy now goes to your computers by itself. You can turn Wireless debugging off: paste-get turns it on for a moment when it needs it, on Wi-Fi.
Shizuku works too, but it has to be started again after each restart of the phone.
Without the automatic copy, send what you copied with the Quick Settings tile, the button on paste-get\'s home screen, or Share → Send to PC.
Until then, send by hand: the Quick Settings tile, or Share → Send to PC.
Android only lets the app in front read the clipboard. paste-get reads it through Shizuku, a free app that lends it the rights of the shell.
Shizuku isn\'t running. Start it again after each restart of the phone.
Shizuku is running. Allow paste-get to use it.
Shizuku can\'t watch the clipboard on this phone: %s
Shizuku stops at each restart of the phone. To go on sending copies meanwhile, paste-get needs two permissions Shizuku can grant now: reading the system log, and showing a window over other apps.
Ready for when Shizuku stops: log access and overlay allowed
For when Shizuku stops, allow paste-get to display over other apps.
Meanwhile, paste-get reads copies another way, once you open it after a restart of the phone.
Meanwhile, paste-get reads copies another way. If Android asks, allow paste-get to access the device logs.
To read each copy, a window shows for a moment, which may close the keyboard. Shizuku avoids that.
Android shows it after each copy sent. This is Android\'s own switch: it hides the notice for every app, not only paste-get. Turn it back on here or in Settings → Privacy.
Android shows \"Shell pasted from your clipboard\" after each copy sent. To hide it, turn off Show clipboard access in Settings → Privacy (it applies to every app).
Android didn\'t let paste-get change this setting: use Settings → Privacy instead
Codes from SMS and apps go to your computer\'s clipboard: just paste them
Only the code leaves the phone, marked as secret, never the message. Computers keep it out of their clipboard history.
To find codes, paste-get needs to read notifications.
Android 15 hides codes from apps that read notifications. paste-get can be allowed to see them through the built-in mode or Shizuku.
If Android says the setting is restricted: in App info, tap ⋮, then Allow restricted settings, and try again.
Turn on Send what you copy with the built-in mode (or Shizuku), then come back here.
It no longer receives your copies. To use it again, pair again from paste-get.
paste-get is free, with no ads and no data collection. If it helps you, a small donation keeps it going.
Open paste-get to send what you copy again
